system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks for mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Refine label-restricted patch pseudo-masks by majority voting inside SLIC superpixels of the raw image before using them as Dice and Focal targets.
HYPOTHESIS: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks raise pseudo-mask Dice against true masks by at least 8 points over raw patch pseudo-masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and MVFA trained on them reaches at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities, versus at most 80% for raw patch pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type for seg_adapters: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks (problem rule); superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks with n_segments in {100, 200, 400}. Snapping: a superpixel is labelled anomalous if the area-weighted mean of the upsampled patch anomaly indicator inside it exceeds 0.5 and the image is labelled abnormal; normal images stay empty. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU vs. true masks, pixel AUROC and Dice of the trained model on held-out masked modalities, and boundary F1 (2-pixel tolerance).
RATIONALE: Patch-level pseudo-masks are 17x17 at 240 px, so each label covers a 14-pixel block and boundaries are wrong almost everywhere along a lesion; Dice supervision on such blocks teaches the adapters blocky maps. MLCA shows that raw-input detail matters for MVFA-style localisation. A cheap way to inject raw detail into the targets is to snap the patch pseudo-mask to image superpixels, so every pseudo-mask boundary follows an intensity edge.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute the problem's label-restricted patch rule (level-4 features, 99th percentile of normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation) giving a 17x17 binary map per abnormal image. 2) Upsample bilinearly to 240x240 to obtain an indicator a(x). 3) Run skimage.segmentation.slic(image, n_segments=200, compactness=10, channel_axis=None for grey images) on the 240x240 input. 4) For superpixel S: label = 1 if mean_{x in S} a(x) > 0.5. 5) Remove components smaller than 20 pixels. 6) dataset/medical_zero.py reads these masks for all datasets marked pseudo; train_zero.py keeps Focal + Dice unchanged. 7) n_segments selected on source validation by pseudo-mask Dice where masks exist in the source fold (never the target). Hyper-parameters otherwise as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs).
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks; snapped pseudo-masks (n_segments 100/200/400); masks removed from 1 and from all 3 masked sources. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU/boundary F1; trained-model pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if snapping does not raise pseudo-mask Dice by 8 points or the trained model's pixel AUROC is not higher than with raw patch pseudo-masks.

Idea B:
TITLE: Boundary-ignored pseudo-mask supervision with a superpixel-consistency regulariser
SUMMARY: Instead of refining pseudo-masks, train MVFA's segmentation adapters on raw label-restricted pseudo-masks while ignoring a band around pseudo-mask boundaries and penalising variance of the predicted map inside image superpixels.
HYPOTHESIS: Ignoring a 7-pixel band around pseudo-mask boundaries and adding a superpixel-consistency penalty (lambda = 0.1) lets MVFA trained without masks reach at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities, at least 3 points above training on the same raw pseudo-masks without these two terms, with no change to the pseudo-mask generation.
RATIONALE: Both parents try to fix pseudo-mask shape before training: superpixel snapping moves boundaries to intensity edges, CRF smoothing removes isolated errors. Their common limitation is that any fixed target is still wrong somewhere. A different explanation is that the network does not need correct boundaries in its targets if it is never penalised where targets are unreliable and is encouraged to respect image structure in its own output. Patch pseudo-masks are wrong mostly within one 14-pixel patch of their boundary (a verified consequence of MVFA's 17x17 grid at 240 px), so ignoring that band removes most label noise; a superpixel-consistency term (inspired by the parents' use of image structure) then lets edges in the raw image shape the prediction. This moves structure from the targets into the loss, which is new relative to both parents.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: label-restricted patch rule (CLIP layer 24, 99th percentile of normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation), upsampled to 240 px (nearest). 2) Ignore band: B = dilate(M, 7 px) XOR erode(M, 7 px); saved with the mask. 3) SLIC superpixels per training image (n_segments 200, compactness 10), saved as label maps. 4) train_zero.py: seg loss = Focal + Dice over pixels outside B (masked mean), plus lambda * L_sp with L_sp = mean over superpixels S of Var_{x in S}(sigmoid(map(x))), computed on all training images (normal and abnormal). 5) Det branch unchanged. 6) Band width (3, 7, 11 px) and lambda (0.03, 0.1, 0.3) selected on source validation pixel AUROC against pseudo-masks. 7) Other hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs, batch 16 by accumulation).
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw pseudo-masks; + ignore band; + superpixel term; both. Masks removed from 1 and 3 masked sources. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice, boundary F1, image AUROC. Falsified if the combination does not exceed raw pseudo-mask training by at least 3 pixel-AUROC points, or if either term alone accounts for none of the gain.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
